findings.contract: The CLI value is a finite extra-second margin added to scripted waits; capture_run receives a finite effective wait budget. Zero is allowed. Existing finite negative behavior is not newly prohibited; no arbitrary maximum is introduced.
findings.evidence: argparse type=float has no finiteness guard; main creates the NetLog directory and dispatches the effective timeout. capture_run passes that budget to asyncio.wait_for(run.done.wait()).

runtime_reasoning.positive_infinity: wait_for uses call_later, yielding an absolute infinite TimerHandle time. At every finite loop time the due guard is true and this timeout callback is not eligible. Normal done completion or external cancellation can still end the run.
runtime_reasoning.nan: The <=0 guard is false; call_later and TimerHandle accept an unordered NaN time. The due comparison NaN >= finite is false if this handle reaches the heap head; heap ordering and surrounding timers prevent a universal timing claim. It is not a valid finite deadline.
runtime_reasoning.negative_infinity: The nonpositive wait_for fast path applies, rather than a meaningful finite requested margin.
runtime_reasoning.limits: No measured hang, browser failure, exact NaN timing or global run-duration guarantee. The C float parser implementation and Linux installed-runtime bytes were not read or executed.

proposed_regressions.cli_positive_design: Default, zero, ordinary positive and a small finite negative margin should each reach exactly one actual awaited observer with the selected Scenario and exact 0.8 seconds plus the margin (default 60.8); propagate the same sentinel. Zero is not treated as an immediate zero effective budget. No fixture is published by this controlled observation.
proposed_regressions.direct_helper_design: Because two current test callers invoke capture_run directly, validate its finite effective budget before handler/resource acquisition as well. A controlled generate_certificate entry sentinel gives an actual canonical early-entry witness without opening resources. Non-finite inputs must raise ValueError before that witness; finite inputs reach it. This proves validation placement only, not native socket or browser behavior.
proposed_regressions.optional_input: Decimal-overflow text such as --timeout=1e309 may supplement the non-finite cases, after the actual parser regression establishes acceptance; not needed for the minimal three cases.
proposed_regressions.minimal_remedy: Use a standard finite-value check immediately after CLI parse and before any mkdir/dispatch; check capture_run effective budget before entering capture_exception_handler/acquisition. Preserve timeout arithmetic, finite values, scenario operations and existing tests. Document that --timeout is a finite margin, not a global wall-clock limit.
